  Exam Date & Time: 10-Jun-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester Makeup Examination, June -2025  
  APPLIED CRYPTOGRAPHY [IT-3251]  
  Marks: 50                                                                                Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Consider the definition of the expression a mod n also makes perfect sense if n is  
  negative. Determine the following:  
  a. 7 mod 4  
  A)      b. 7 mod -4                                                                                    (5)  
  c. -7 mod 4  
  d. -7 mod -4  
  
  B)      Solvay-Strassen Primality Testing can be slightly more complex and has more error  
  probability than the computations in Miller-Rabin. Justify with an illustration of n=561       (5)  
  
  $$2)           Using the RSA public key cryptosystem, with a = 1, b = 2 . . . y = 25, z = 26.$$  
  $$(a) If p = 5 and q = 13, list two legal values for d.$$  
  $$(b) If p = 5, q = 31, and d = 37, find e.                                                      (5)$$  
  $$A)      (c) Using p = 3, q = 11, and d = 9, find e and encrypt ''hello''.$$  
  
  B)  
  
  
  (5)  
  
  
  3)           Consider a highly simplified RSA cryptosystem applied in the Public switched  
  telephone networks, in which the public key of given user is 31 and n = 3599. Compute  
  (5)  
  the original message sent by the sender for the cipher text "X". Assume [A...Z] = [1..26].  
  A)  
  B)      Investigate the impact of hash collisions on data integrity and security. How does the  
  probability of collisions vary with different hash functions and input data sizes?             (5)  
  
  4)           Explore real-world applications and use cases of digital signatures with a focus on a          (5)  
  specific industry or sector.  
  
  A)      i. Select an industry (e.g., banking, healthcare, legal) and describe how digital signatures  
  are applied to enhance security and efficiency.  
  ii. Provide examples of scenarios where digital signatures facilitate secure transactions,  
  document authentication, or compliance with regulatory requirements.

  iii. Discuss the benefits and challenges associated with digital signature adoption in the  
  chosen industry.  
  
  B)         Two parties agree to use a common shared channel to communicate, in which Alice and  
  Bob use the common prime p = 941 and the primitive root g = 627. Alice chooses the  
  secret key a = 347 and Bob chooses the secret key b = 78. Compute the common shared (5)  
  key used in the commutation.  
  
  5)              A user at a marketing agency, "BuzzBrand," clicks on a suspicious link in a phishing  
  email. The user's computer becomes sluggish, and unexpected pop-up ads start  
  appearing.  
  A)  
  i. What type of malware is most likely infecting the user's computer, based on the  
  symptoms?                                                                                     (5)  
  ii. What information can be gathered from system logs and process monitoring to  
  identify the specific malware?  
  iii. How can antivirus software help detect and prevent malware infections?  
  iv. Describe the steps the IT team should take to respond to this malware infection  
  
  B)         A company manages a network of point-of-sale (POS) terminals that process daily credit  
  card transactions. Security is paramount to protect customer data and prevent financial (5)  
  losses. Analyse which type of IDS is most suitable for this scenario and Justify.  
  
  
  -----End-----
